quote.text: In every walk with nature, one receives far more than he seeks.
quote.author: John Muir

fun_fact.text: In Hungarian, the word for butterfly is 'pillangó' (pronounced pee-lon-go), which comes from an old word meaning 'fluttering.' Hungary is home to over 160 species of butterflies, including the stunning Swallowtail that graces gardens just like yours in summertime!

short_read.title: The Secret Lives of Harbor Seals
short_read.teaser: Harbor seals are regular visitors to the Strait of Juan de Fuca, and they're much more fascinating than you might think. Learn about their underwater singing, their whiskers that detect fish movements, and how they nap while floating upright!

medium_read.title: The Hidden Language of Flowers in Victorian Gardens
medium_read.teaser: Victorians used flowers to send secret messages, and many of the blooms in your garden once had special meanings. Discover what your favorite flowers were 'saying' in the 1800s and how this charming tradition continues today.

long_read.title: The Budapest Coffee House Culture That Shaped a Nation
long_read.teaser: For centuries, Budapest's grand coffee houses were the heart of Hungarian intellectual and artistic life, where writers, poets, and revolutionaries gathered over cakes and coffee. This beautifully illustrated journey explores how these elegant cafés became cultural institutions and many still thrive today.

port_angeles.title: Bald Eagles Nesting Along the Strait
port_angeles.description: August is a wonderful time to spot bald eagles along the Strait of Juan de Fuca, as parent eagles are still teaching their young to fish. Ediz Hook and the waterfront near the ferry terminal are excellent viewing spots, especially in early morning. Bring binoculars and you might see them diving for salmon!

puzzle_1.question: A hummingbird's heart beats about ___ times per minute while in flight.
puzzle_1.correct_response: Exactly right, Barbara! That tiny heart is working incredibly hard to power those amazing wings!
puzzle_1.close_response: You're very close! A hummingbird's heart beats about 1,200 times per minute — your heart is probably beating around 70 times per minute right now!
puzzle_1.wrong_response: These tiny dynamos have hearts that beat about 1,200 times per minute! That's roughly 20 beats every single second to fuel their incredible hovering flight.
puzzle_1.learn_more_text: Hummingbirds have the fastest metabolism of any bird, and their hearts can even beat faster — up to 1,260 times per minute — when they're especially active. At night when they sleep, their heart rate drops to about 50 beats per minute to conserve energy.

puzzle_2.question: Which Hungarian word means 'welcome'?
puzzle_2.correct_response: Isten hozta — exactly right! This beautiful phrase literally means 'God brought you' and is such a warm way to welcome someone.
puzzle_2.wrong_response: The answer is 'Isten hozta' — what a lovely phrase! It literally means 'God brought you,' making every guest feel truly meant to be there. (Köszönöm means thank you, Viszlát means goodbye, and Jó reggelt means good morning.)
puzzle_2.learn_more_text: Hungarian greetings are often quite poetic. While 'Isten hozta' is traditional, Hungarians also use 'Isten hozott' for welcoming one person or 'Isten hozta' for multiple people, showing respect through grammar itself.

puzzle_3.question: What special ability do sea otters have that helps them stay warm in cold Pacific waters?
options: They migrate to warmer waters in winter
They have the densest fur of any animal
They can heat their bodies like electric blankets
puzzle_3.correct_response: Wonderful! Sea otters have the densest fur of any animal — up to one million hairs per square inch! That's why you often see them grooming so carefully, keeping air trapped in their fur for insulation.
puzzle_3.wrong_response: Sea otters actually have the densest fur of any animal on Earth — up to one million hairs per square inch! Unlike seals and whales, they don't have blubber, so they rely entirely on their incredibly thick fur coat and must groom it constantly to stay warm in our cold waters.
puzzle_3.learn_more_text: Sea otters spend a huge portion of their day grooming their fur to maintain its insulating properties. They also have a super-fast metabolism and must eat about 25% of their body weight in food each day to stay warm!
